h: From PG Tips Chimps to Shrovetide Football
p: Twycross has a back story that older visitors will remember fondly. It was founded in 1963 by Molly Badham and Nathalie Evans, and for years its chimpanzees starred in the much-loved PG Tips tea adverts on telly. These days the zoo is very much a conservation charity, with a serious focus on primates and endangered species, but that bit of TV nostalgia still raises a smile with grandparents on a day out.

A few tips for a smoother visit. Grab a map as you arrive and plan your route around the talks and feeding times you most want to catch, as it's easy to miss them if you just drift. Bring a picnic if you want to keep costs down, and pack waterproofs even if the morning looks bright, because a Midlands shower can sneak up on you mid-afternoon. With toddlers, a buggy is a good shout as the distances soon add up.

Atherstone is a small, historic market town on the old Roman road of Watling Street, once famous for hat making. It's best known for its Shrovetide Ball Game, a chaotic, centuries-old street football match held every Shrove Tuesday, when the town boards up its shop windows and crowds battle over an oversized leather ball. Not one for the faint-hearted, but brilliant to watch.

Nearby, the Bosworth Battlefield Heritage Centre near Market Bosworth tells the story of the 1485 battle where Richard III lost his crown, while the Ashby Canal and the Battlefield Line heritage railway at Shackerstone offer gentler ways to explore the countryside.
